name: Signal generator
description: A function generator channel: a sine, square or triangle wave set by frequency, amplitude and offset, or an arbitrary wave made of samples repeated over a period. It is an ideal voltage source between its output and common terminals, stepped on the clock of the MCU: a sine or a triangle is held for one sixty-fourth of its period at a time, a square wave changes at its two edges, an arbitrary wave holds each sample for period / count. Common must be tied to a reference (the ground rail or another source). The limits (voltage, frequency, time resolution) are published with the circuit view, and a request beyond them is refused before it takes effect.

waveform.description: 0: sine, 1: square, 2: triangle, 3: arbitrary (samples programmed with the circuit API or a scenario step).

frequency.description: Frequency of a sine, square or triangle wave, in hertz. The highest value also depends on the MCU clock: the steps cannot be closer than 16 clock cycles.

amplitude.description: Peak amplitude of a sine, square or triangle wave, in volts.

offset.description: Voltage added to the wave, in volts.

duty.description: Share of the period a square wave spends high, in percent.

period.description: Period over which the samples of an arbitrary wave repeat, in seconds.

enabled.description: The channel output. Off, the terminals are left open. Enabling starts the wave at its first sample.

sampleCount.description: Number of samples of the arbitrary wave.

currentLimit.description: Current the output is rated for, in amperes: asking for more is reported as an overload, the voltage is still held.

setpoint.description: Voltage the generator holds at this instant, in volts.

outputVoltage.description: Voltage obtained between the terminals, in volts.

outputCurrent.description: Current delivered by the output terminal, in amperes (negative when it absorbs current).
